composition.observation: The Desktop Bedroom remains at the same position and scale underneath the floating Assistant. The Properties pane remains available at right.

hierarchy.observation: The upper bar names the working Scene and saved revision. The Library uses a named object card, with Scene graph and Properties taking over the dock when selected.

typography.observation: The larger Assistant prompt and named Properties headings stand apart from the smaller working status and model details. On mobile the Treasure chest description and floor support measurement wrap inside their card.

spacing.observation: Desktop leaves a clear canvas between the Library and Properties, while mobile dedicates the width to its active dock instead of compressing desktop columns.

controls.observation: The treasure chest has an explicit Add to active Scene button. Dock assistance exchanges its label for Float assistance, with View canvas remaining separately available.

contrast.observation: Light labels and blue focus strokes remain distinct against the dark navy work area, and the brown chest is visible against the pale Bedroom floor.

consistency.observation: The Library, graph, and Inspector keep the same blue panel family and use matching outlined controls. Switching Library categories does not move the top-level editing controls.

states.observation: The model appears in the room and as a counted graph item after Add. A private composition is then searchable under My Creations and the reused item exposes editable Properties.

responsive.observation: On mobile, Assistant and authoring docks occupy most of the narrow canvas width with distinct paths back to View canvas and the left rail.

keyboard.observation: The Scene graph describes Space and Shift range selection and the outline identifies the active Float assistance control. The mobile recording shows focus traversing category and filter controls.

focus.observation: Entry brings a blue outline to the Parallax heading, and docking leaves an outline on Float assistance, so the current control is evident after transition.

feedback.observation: Adding the chest updates the canvas, active Properties heading and graph count. The later mobile footage displays the composition saved notice before returning to the private Library results.

motion.observation: Desktop normal footage shows the Assistant over the existing canvas and then being removed without a canvas jump. Mobile reduced footage moves among the dock, Library and Properties without an obstructive transition.

continuity.observation: Desk Map and its revision remain visible through Assistant reveal and dock. Reused composition remains editable independently. The exact-source SC02 supplemental replay also reopened the same saved Scene.

complexity.observation: An unavailable Assistant leaves View canvas and the ordinary editor available. Built-in versus My Creations is exposed as a Library filter instead of mixing model and saved-composition ownership.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator opens Spatial Studio through Studio, keeps the scene when using assistance, places the modeled chest, saves and reuses a composition, and returns to the Creator Library.

fallbacks.observation: When Spatial Assistant is unavailable, the notice says scenes are safe and editing can continue. Send idea is visually disabled while the canvas and manual selection remain available.

findings.observation: The SC02 capture proves private save and editable reuse; the earlier independent pass still needed direct proof of same-Scene and effect persistence after reload.
findings.resolution: The current mobile recording shows independent composition edits before leaving the editor. The exact-source supplemental Chromium case in .cache/homeport-depth-reload-current.log explicitly reopened the same Scene and passed its real asset, light editing and composition reuse checks including reload.

composition.observation: The review remains a single, focused blue dialog over the Studio. Narrow screens retain an independently scrolling body and a separate stable action footer.

hierarchy.observation: The missing Profile prerequisite comes before the saved source on mobile. On Review entry the server verification label, focused heading, and immutable release warning appear before package details or Submit.

typography.observation: Both screens use a distinct title, compact step names, and readable body copy for visibility and licensing. The review heading remains legible under its focus outline.

spacing.observation: The step list wraps without hiding a stage, and the bottom footer separates Back, stage number, and the primary control from the vertically stacked disclosures.

controls.observation: Continue is disabled before a public Profile exists and turns active after return. Review package stays gated by rights confirmation, and Submit has a different label and its own stage.

contrast.observation: The cyan focus outline and amber warning card remain distinguishable against the navy pane. Disabled Continue has a visibly lower emphasis than enabled Continue.

consistency.observation: The same five stages, warning highlight treatment, and distinction between private source and separately moderated package appear in both desktop and mobile dialog captures.

states.observation: Profile required, restored ready, server included content, rights review, package reviewed and returned are visually distinct. No submitted or public state appears in this journey.

responsive.observation: Mobile stages and explanations wrap inside the dialog. Most importantly, the review entry keeps the heading and full first warning on screen with the footer still reachable.

keyboard.observation: The recording shows the redistribution checkbox with a focus outline before review. After activation, focus goes to Review before submitting rather than forcing a tab into the footer.

focus.observation: At 15.35 seconds the mobile recording is down at the checked rights control; at 15.65 seconds the focus outline surrounds Review before submitting near the top of the content pane.

feedback.observation: The package explicitly distinguishes the currently inspected saved revision and server-reviewed asset, explains moderation, and separately warns that the source has no pinned Environment.

motion.observation: The reduced-motion recording shows the rights checkbox and bottom scroll offset replaced by the immediately visible focus target and caution on the new stage, with no extra user scroll.

continuity.observation: The same revision 3 named Scene appears on both sides of Profile setup and in the Included content card. Back in the Studio Library the selected card still says Private creation and no Community listing.

complexity.observation: Rights and redistribution are grouped before a dedicated verification pane. Profile setup is linked directly at the gate, and the five steps keep each decision in context.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator discovers the named private saved Scene, restores Profile eligibility, inspects actual included content and the server-reviewed package, and returns without creating a listing.

fallbacks.observation: Missing Profile gives an explicit reason and direct setup link with the source remaining private. The reviewed package makes the observed unpinned Environment fallback to a Spatial asset explicit.

findings.observation: The earlier mobile capture carried the lower Rights scroll position into Review and initially hid its heading and immutable-release warning.
findings.resolution: At 15.35 seconds the current recording is scrolled to the checked Rights control. At 15.65 seconds Review has entered and its heading is focused, with all of the first immutable-release warning visible before any subsequent interaction. Desktop shows the same heading and initial warning above its action footer.

composition.observation: The Daily AI activity card sits directly under comparison. Desktop places the selector at upper right, and mobile moves it into the normal reading order above the data.

hierarchy.observation: The chart title, labeled selector, UTC explanatory text and corresponding totals form a clear sequence. The dossier gives the selected person their own prominent page title.

typography.observation: Compact uppercase UTC and metric labels clearly separate metadata from body copy; roomier serif headings mark the distinct Daily AI activity and People sections.

spacing.observation: The unit definitions and stacked controls fit mobile independently of the horizontal comparison table. The narrow identifier strip is noticeably more crowded than desktop.

controls.observation: The same select returns from settled and accounted cost to Requests per day. The canonical People flow opens the named Dossier with scoped allowance controls and a clear return.

contrast.observation: The gold focus outline around the select and bright frame on the People return heading remain distinct on the dark green field.

consistency.observation: The Chartroom cards and Safe return action persist across usage, dossier, and People search, with common status badges and borders.

states.observation: Settled cost, accounted exposure and admitted requests display three distinct selector values and explanations. The safely empty month displays zero rather than invented bars.

responsive.observation: On mobile the table is contained in its own labeled horizontal scroll area and the chart selector is fully in view. The account identifier line crowds the right edge.

keyboard.observation: The mobile chart video shows the comparison table take focus and labels its horizontal-navigation instructions. The dossier video shows visible focus reaching the exception expiry control.

focus.observation: The selection keeps focus on Chart shows, while return from the Dossier puts the visible outline on People.

feedback.observation: Chart mode changes immediately replace both the selected metric and its explanatory sentence, including the distinction between settled cost and pending reservations.

motion.observation: Reduced mobile footage shows settled/accounted/request transitions as direct selector updates, and dossier return reveals the People heading without requiring a separate viewport adjustment.

continuity.observation: Mode changes keep the month and chart context stable. The named Dossier is reached through People, and return lands back on the known-clue People search.

complexity.observation: A single selector avoids spreading daily metrics across separate pages. People search explains its bounded, non-enumerating behavior in the empty state.

role-outcomes.observation: The Administrator compares daily cost definitions and reaches the intended person’s inherited allowance fields through canonical People search, then leaves without changing policy.

fallbacks.observation: The empty chart reports zero requests and zero settled cost with clear UTC context. Empty People asks for a known clue instead of displaying a directory.

findings.observation: The narrow identity strip leaves little room for the account identifier and the desktop Copy control is outside the captured mobile row. The selected identity and allowance controls are readable and the return works.

composition.observation: The Overview and AI Usage pages preserve separate headings within the same Chartroom shell, with economics filters grouped above view tabs and the detailed trends below.

hierarchy.observation: Date and filter controls appear before detailed capability sections. The Quality over time heading introduces a separate per-capability disclosure and explicit availability text.

typography.observation: The large serif page title and smaller section hierarchy distinguish the overview from AI Usage. Small metric labels are paired with readable values such as Unavailable and zero recorded attempts.

spacing.observation: Desktop holds the dates, capability, model and action in a compact horizontal group. Mobile uses two columns and then puts Apply economics filters on its own row.

controls.observation: Preset dates, paired UTC input fields, filters and the persistent tab bar remain distinct from the Quality disclosure and operation-trace filters.

contrast.observation: The cyan focus stroke of the active disclosure and amber tab/filter outline are distinguishable against the deep green interface.

consistency.observation: The station shell, date values and filter labels remain consistent when jumping from Economics to Quality, Capabilities, and History and back.

states.observation: Platform Overview and AI Usage are different visible destinations. The disclosure shows no dated operations for the fixture, and History shows its explicit empty state.

responsive.observation: The narrow view’s tab buttons wrap into pairs with Operation History full width. The sticky masthead overlaps the top of the scrolled hero in some captures, while current tab and working controls stay usable.

keyboard.observation: The mobile recording shows focused date editing and visible focus among navigation tabs and operation filters. The Quality trend summary can be focused and opened.

focus.observation: The opened Quality trend outline stays on its summary and the return leaves an unmistakable outline on Overview.

feedback.observation: Empty evidence is labeled No dated operations, Unavailable or No AI operations rather than appearing as fabricated trends. Date boundaries and evidence coverage are explained inline.

motion.observation: The reduced recording shows the Platform Overview, analysis tabs, and return as direct view changes with immediate readable state and retained filters.

continuity.observation: The date range and filter selections remain the same after switching into separate views and returning to Overview. The persistent header keeps the same Safe return route available.

complexity.observation: The first view exposes period/capability choices while detailed quality definitions and tracing are progressively disclosed in their own tab or card.

role-outcomes.observation: The Administrator goes to Platform Overview through the shell, enters economics, inspects capability quality and recorded-operation history, then returns to the cost overview.

fallbacks.observation: The captured empty period has honest no-operations and no-trend messages plus a route to try another period. The synthetic capture does not exercise a network refresh failure or a populated trend.

composition.observation: On desktop the bedroom keeps the size and visual framing seen before launch while the floating panel covers the left side. Docking relocates the panel toward the Inspector. On mobile it occupies most of the narrow editor and includes View canvas in the panel.

hierarchy.observation: The window title leads the header, the transient move or resize acknowledgment sits beside Dock assistance, and the Desk Map context strip separates both from the composer and prompt cards.

typography.observation: The large serif prompt heads the assistant body while the window title and controls use distinct, readable sans-serif weights. The compact confirmation text remains legible at mobile working size.

spacing.observation: On the phone the header wraps the title above the control row, which leaves a gap between Window resized and Dock assistance. Move and resize retain the editor window edges, input, and both footer actions within the viewport.

controls.observation: Dock assistance becomes Float assistance on docking. Close, View canvas, the lower-right resize handle and the focusable title remain separate from Start new task and Send idea.

contrast.observation: White status text sits on the same dark blue header as the title. The pale outline around the move handle and around Float assistance stays visible against the button and panel surfaces.

consistency.observation: Desk Map and the dark Studio colors carry through open, resized, moved and docked states. Returning switches to the existing green Library shell while retaining the signed-in identity, matching the reference emphasis on contextual navigation.

states.observation: Opening, resized, moved and docked are visually distinct. The resize acknowledgment changes to Window moved when the header receives the arrow action, then Float assistance replaces the dock control and the stale status clears.

responsive.observation: The full assistant and an unobscured section of the bedroom share the desktop canvas. On mobile the assistant is almost full width, with reachable View canvas and both composer actions still inside the viewport after the move and resize.

keyboard.observation: The recorded journey exercises ArrowLeft on the bottom-right resize handle and ArrowRight on the separately focusable title. Desktop and mobile reduced recordings both show feedback after the arrow operations.

focus.observation: The lower-right resize corner has its own focus indicator. Focus visibly moves to the assistant title for movement and to Float assistance for the docked state.

feedback.observation: Window resized and Window moved are printed explicitly in the panel header on desktop and phone. Outcome timing in the four contexts peaks at 983 ms against the 3000 ms contract budget.

motion.observation: Normal desktop frames show the open panel at five seconds, resized panel at seven, docked panel at eleven and unobscured editor before the return. Reduced mobile shows resize and move states with visible confirmations during the same short interaction sequence.

continuity.observation: Desk Map and Working draft saved revision 1 remain in the desktop context through movement and docking. Both captures return to the same Creator Studio Library with its account chip still present.

complexity.observation: The inverse Dock and Float controls share one location and the prompt controls stay at the bottom. The lower-right resize affordance is less prominent than Dock assistance but its visible focused corner distinguishes it from composer controls.

role-outcomes.observation: The authenticated Creator opens Spatial Studio, opens assistance, moves and resizes it with readable acknowledgments, docks and closes it, and returns to the same Library account.

fallbacks.observation: The assistant reports that it is unavailable and that scenes are safe for manual editing. Its disabled send action leaves View canvas and Close assistance available, and the desktop recording shows the unobscured bedroom after closing.

findings.observation: Moving and resizing do not show the required visible confirmation on desktop or phone. Both recordings show only small geometry changes and focus styling. The runtime snapshot places the exact confirmation text in an aria-live screen-reader-only span, and the journey asserts the enclosing region instead of the confirmation itself. Keep the accessible announcement and render a visible acknowledgment that the test can assert directly.
findings.resolution: Both normal sizes show the literal Window resized and Window moved statuses in the header. The reduced-motion phone recording shows those same states, and the docked panel clears the previous acknowledgment.

composition.observation: Desktop keeps Scene graph, bedroom and Inspector visible as the rail changes destinations. On mobile the active Inspector occupies the available width beneath the Studio toolbar and the destination rail remains alongside it.

hierarchy.observation: Each destination starts with a unique heading and the same selected object name. Properties puts immediate object actions above identity and shape, while Spatial context uses the same header space and introduces placement and relationships underneath.

typography.observation: Larger Desk Map and panel headings anchor each view. Smaller section labels, companion descriptions and units distinguish the editable fields from labels without hiding the clue text on the phone.

spacing.observation: Dividers separate identity, shape, placement and relationship groups. The mobile scrollable pane leaves room for full-width recovery buttons and prevents their labels from colliding with the surrounding rail.

controls.observation: Properties includes Frame, Hide, Lock, Duplicate, and Delete, with independent fields for the object identity and shape. Spatial context adds its own placement selector and layer controls while Scene settings provides an experience title and Guided fallback field.

contrast.observation: The white panel and object titles contrast with the dark blue fills. The active rail outline, readable form values and light borders on Undo last edit make position and the recovery action distinguishable in the narrow layout.

consistency.observation: Object name, clue and action placement persist from Properties to Spatial context. The Studio return recovers the familiar Library layout and account identity on both widths, in keeping with the reference's distinct destinations.

states.observation: Scene settings, Properties and Spatial context each show their own usable content. Removing the duplicate yields a Selection unavailable panel with recovery choices. Undo restores Properties for Desk Map copy with the existing clue text.

responsive.observation: The desktop layout preserves the graph and full preview beside the Inspector. The mobile layout keeps the Inspector readable as a dedicated pane with its controls stacked, and the return shell fits the phone without requiring the desktop rail.

keyboard.observation: The primary rail captures show visible destinations and the exact-source SC-00B supplemental Chromium test exercises keyboard rail navigation while preserving depth and the selected typed effect. The main capture uses rail clicks.

focus.observation: The active or focused rail destination has a bright outline on desktop and phone. After the missing-selection recovery, the mobile Properties destination clearly identifies the restored object.

feedback.observation: The missing-selection view explains what happened and immediately offers Undo last edit, Open scene settings and a remaining Desk Map choice. The restored panel names Desk Map copy. The recorded action-to-heading measurements peak at 152 ms.

motion.observation: The normal desktop recording shows the duplicate selected before returning and the reduced-motion mobile recording transitions from loading to distinct rail destinations without a long animation. The four removal contexts and four rail contexts all reach their outcomes.

continuity.observation: Properties and Spatial context retain Desk Map selection. The deletion and undo pair restore the duplicate and clue before the return, and the account indicator remains on the same Library destination.

complexity.observation: The three-destination rail avoids mixing scene-wide fields with object edits. The exact-source light-theme sequence keeps Soft mist selected when moving from Guided's basic viewport tools to Standard's coordinate selector and Engineering's grid and coordinate readout.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator opens individual object tools, contextual tools and scene-wide controls under the same draft. The removal journey gives the Creator a reversible recovery path with the original object still available.

fallbacks.observation: The current renderer-disabled desktop screenshot shows Retry 3D renderer and offers the scene hierarchy, precise Inspector controls and Guided View. Desktop Properties retains the Desk Map clue at revision 1, mobile Spatial context retains the same object and manual placement details, and both supplemental runs verify the Library return.

findings.observation: The captured Inspector journeys demonstrate Guided rendering and object removal recovery. They do not show Standard or Engineering depth, or the Inspector and its draft history with the renderer unavailable. The promised presentation changes and renderer-loss fallback need exact-candidate rendered evidence.
findings.resolution: The exact-source SC-00B Chromium test passed and its rendered light-theme Guided, Standard and Engineering screenshots retain Soft mist while adding the World coordinates selector and Engineering grid and coordinate readout. The exact-source renderer-disabled desktop Properties screenshot retains Desk Map and its existing clue beside the 3D unavailable notice. The phone Spatial context screenshot retains Desk Map and its manual placement controls. Both renderer-disabled journeys passed and verified the same Library return.

composition.observation: The upper editor distinguishes the shared Environment from the Desk Map Scene and leaves the canvas as the main content. Small dorm is a tighter furnished volume, while the trail and plaza are landscape layouts rather than variations of the bedroom shell.

hierarchy.observation: Preview and Environment selectors sit above the canvas. Surfaces adds a named picker inside the preview, followed by the wall snap outcome and saved revision, rather than obscuring which environment or scene is being authored.

typography.observation: The preview names and saved-draft revision are readable at normal working size. On the phone, Room surfaces and short labels such as Entire floor, wall left and desk chair seat remain identifiable in the compact picker.

spacing.observation: The desktop picker fits near the scene edge with the Inspector in its own column. The mobile picker wraps into rows within the viewport without horizontal clipping. The empty and cluttered rooms remain framed to show their footprints.

controls.observation: The dedicated overlay toggle opens named surface buttons, with explicit blocked labels where relevant. Environment remains a separate selector. The selected wall focus and manual-placement footer mark which control produced the result.

contrast.observation: The translucent blue plane overlay is distinct from the cool wall and pale floor, while active control outlines look brighter than the dark dock. The yellow clue mark on the snapped mobile wall is visible but less salient than the focused button and revision change.

consistency.observation: Bedroom, Classroom, Gallery and Plaza change their geometry and preview name while retaining the same toolbar, Desk Map identity and editor frame. The Library return restores its familiar account shell rather than leaving the Creator in a new navigation context.

states.observation: The surface-ready view outlines planes and exposes the named picker, and the snapped view shows an applied mark and revision 2. All ten named previews include visibly different layouts. Empty room has the shell plus the authored clue mark, while Cluttered room has boxes and furniture.

responsive.observation: On desktop the preview shares the frame with Properties. On mobile the compact toolbar and lower picker stay inside the viewport, and living room, gallery, trail and empty room are still recognizable as distinct compositions.

keyboard.observation: The declared visible Environment control uses Home, arrow and Enter selection, with each new selected environment and matching Preview label visible in the recordings. Surface activation itself uses the named wall action.

focus.observation: The Surfaces button shows a visible focus ring on the phone when opening and after snapping. After selection changes, the Environment selector stays outlined while the canvas updates underneath.

feedback.observation: The desktop caption confirms that Desk Map snapped and aligned to wall left. The mobile capture shows the clue mark fixed on that wall and the saved revision advances to 2. Each named preview updates the selector and canvas label together.

motion.observation: Desktop video shows the surface picker, the applied wall placement, the reframed classroom and plaza, and the Library return. Reduced mobile video shows the matching applied wall, Office and Empty room states. The largest recorded action-to-feedback boundary is 1491 ms against 3000 ms.

continuity.observation: Preview changes keep the same Desk Map and saved revision 2, including the authored clue on the empty room wall. Both device outcomes return to the same Creator Studio Library.

complexity.observation: Surface choice is grouped into a single named picker with unavailable surfaces separately marked. The same Environment selector switches between rooms, so no second tool or divergent layout is needed for the trail and plaza.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator enters the draft, exposes whole wall and floor surfaces, applies the left-wall placement, views all ten named previews and returns to the same Library. This bounded product review does not certify physical geometry tolerances or renderer cost.

fallbacks.observation: Manual placement guidance, selectable room surfaces and visible authored placement work with the background indicator showing AI unavailable on desktop. The reduced journey remains usable with the same native selector and return action.

composition.observation: Desktop keeps the cutaway bedroom between the Library and Inspector and reserves a lower work area for Simulation. The phone trades the side panels for one narrow pane and shows the canvas again after the Library closes.

hierarchy.observation: The Spatial Library shows the Assets tab, search field and selected visual card before the release selector and placement actions; Simulation keeps its state explanation next to its interaction controls.

typography.observation: The selected reusable clue has a distinct title, a separate Classification line and Version 1.0.0 in a labeled selector. The phone card's title and action labels are readable at the recorded width.

spacing.observation: On the phone, the asset details pair Open original with publishing and Place in Scene with Create independent copy, with space between rows. The compact Simulation dock has less space for adjacent tab names once reset gains focus.

controls.observation: The clearly labeled Place in Scene action opens a named placement prompt with Floor and Cancel placement. Simulation offers Simulate inspect and Reset simulation in the same dock while previewing the scene.

contrast.observation: Pale text, a bright active border and the dark Library cards separate title, metadata and actions. The small desktop Preview quality label has low contrast over the pale room wall even though the Medium control stays readable.

consistency.observation: Both devices use the same room schematic, saved asset status, explicit placement controls and blue-toned surfaces. Both show the same room and return through Creator Studio to the green Chronicle Library shell.

states.observation: Saved asset, inspected released version, placement prompt and working-draft revision 2 are visibly separate. Simulation also distinguishes the no-match response and the initial state restored by reset.

responsive.observation: At phone width the details read vertically and the scene placement prompt fits inside the canvas while retaining Floor and Cancel placement. After focusing Reset the tab strip partially clips Simulation and Events, though the action and result remain visible.

keyboard.observation: The Library journey exercises Home in the category flow and uses labeled search and placement controls. The reduced phone recording shows source-to-placement navigation; it does not enumerate all shortcuts advertised for group editing.

focus.observation: The selected reusable card has a visible outline and the Reset simulation button receives a conspicuous double focus ring on the phone. The relative placement prompt keeps its selectable Floor action in view.

feedback.observation: The Simulation dock exposes the no-match explanation and reset text. Placement advances the saved working revision. Browser measurements for these journeys range from about 123 to 431 ms, within the 3000 ms contract.

motion.observation: The sampled normal desktop run changes the evaluation and resets at the same work surface; the reduced phone run retains the same reset text and return despite the different motion preference.

continuity.observation: After placing into Desk Map, the editor shows revision 2 with the working scene still selected and retains the synthetic Creator on the return screen. Simulation reset explicitly says Chronicle progress is unchanged.

complexity.observation: Search narrows the Assets gallery to a single named definition and a focused details panel holds version and copy actions. Simulation keeps inspect and reset beside a short explanation instead of exposing all authoring details at once.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator saves a distinct named reusable clue, selects version 1.0.0, places a copy in the existing scene and returns. The second journey diagnoses the unmatched Inspect interaction and restores the initial state.

fallbacks.observation: The capture shows ordinary asset and simulation controls usable in the synthetic fixture. The no-effect state explains why the interaction changed nothing and offers Reset; guided placement presents Floor and Cancel. Native and production AI fallbacks are outside this rendered journey.

findings.observation: At phone width the focused selected Simulation tab is readable on entry. After focusing the interaction or reset, the tab strip shows only the end of Simulation and part of Events next to the fixed transport controls in both motion modes. Reset remains reachable and its confirmation is visible, but the active dock and adjacent destinations are harder to identify.

A reusable Clue in the Assets tab is labeled Saved asset on its card and metadata, but the details say Creator-owned spatial Scene. The wording muddies the definition/scene distinction even though the release and explicit placement actions work.
With the desktop Library and Inspector open, the Preview quality label lies partly over a pale wall and loses legibility. Its Medium selector keeps a solid background and remains legible.

composition.observation: The wide editor puts shared Environment and active Scene in a single briefing strip above the canvas. A bounded dialog overlays the scene and organizes creation, the gallery and revision impact; the phone uses the same content in one vertical pane.

hierarchy.observation: Environments & Scenes is the dialog title, followed by the explanation of independent Scene content and the current Environment. The impact section differentiates the selected Environment version, Scene names, status and update actions.

typography.observation: On the phone the title wraps to two lines without crowding the Close control. The impact card uses bold Scene titles and visible CURRENT or REVIEW REQUIRED labels above quieter revision and explanation text.

spacing.observation: The desktop gallery gives cards individual room for schematic, metadata and buttons. On the phone each Environment review entry has its own spacing and dividing line, and the long dialog uses vertical scrolling to reach successive sections.

controls.observation: The dialog distinguishes Edit shared Environment from Scene creation and renaming. There is an explicit Update and revalidate control per Scene, and the compare selector and Compare Scenes action appear together.

contrast.observation: Light headings and blue-outlined buttons read on dark panels. The filled blue explanation panel separates shared context from controls, and the disabled current-scene update button is visually quieter than available updates.

consistency.observation: Desktop and mobile repeat the same Editor and dialog terms, Scene schematic cards, saved version labels and per-Scene controls. The independent Environment edit opens the familiar blue renderer and uses Back to scene.

states.observation: The review shows the saved Environment, three named working Scenes with distinct contents, a duplicate promoted to The Letter Study and finally Ordinary Room CURRENT while neighbors remain REVIEW REQUIRED.

responsive.observation: At phone width create fields stack, selectable controls stay within the dialog and the full review list can be reached vertically. Desktop keeps the thumbnail gallery wider and can expose several Scenes at once.

keyboard.observation: The replay exercises Home, ArrowDown and Enter on native Scene starting-content, preview lighting and comparison selectors. The recordings show the later concrete effects of those choices, including populated scene cards and a chosen comparison. Escape and exhaustive trap traversal are outside these captured steps.

focus.observation: Opening the manager leaves Close visibly focused in the top section. The phone’s Review Environment impact button shows a distinct focus outline before the per-scene changes.

feedback.observation: Creation notices identify distinct independent working Scenes. Revalidation changes Ordinary Room to CURRENT while neighboring rows remain pending and the Comparison results call out a content difference. Measured feedback ranges from about 1495 to 1712 ms against 3000 ms.

motion.observation: Sampled normal desktop and reduced-motion phone clips retain the sequence from Scene creation through duplicate and revision review to Creator Studio. The important dialog and review states remain present after transitions.

continuity.observation: The shared Environment stays The Haunted Bedroom while the active Scene changes. The impact list keeps published versions pinned as explained in the UI. The same Creator returns to the main Studio shell after the review.

complexity.observation: Creation, gallery, active scene, impact and compare are labeled areas of one dialog. It is long on phone, but the per-scene impact groups are explicitly named and share the same action phrasing, while semantic references can stay collapsed.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator saves an owned Environment, creates three distinct Scenes, duplicates and renames one, reviews a newer shared revision and updates only Ordinary Room before comparing it with The Letter Study. The pending names in the impact list make the separation observable.

fallbacks.observation: In the captured working renderer, gallery schematics and textual scene identity, status and comparison provide non-visual-model cues. Missing 3D, physical reconstruction and scene rendering were not exercised by this particular journey.

composition.observation: Desktop keeps the cutaway Bedroom next to the spatial Inspector; mobile switches the central space between the room and an Inspector, preserving the rails and the important room and Scene identities.

hierarchy.observation: The Inspector starts by identifying the editable Bedroom, then moves to New desk as its main heading when that feature is selected. Its controls and the explanation of generic geometry are immediately below.

typography.observation: Bedroom, New desk and the properties labels remain distinct. On phone Field name and Classification are separated from the current values, and the geometry provenance appears in smaller readable text.

spacing.observation: The selector and name fields fit the panel width; Move and Rotate stay together while Resize wraps onto a separate line on the phone. Desktop gives the viewport and properties panel their own columns.

controls.observation: Room features has a labeled selector and separate transform, name and classification controls. The mobile capture also exposes Rebuild generic feature shape under Classification.

contrast.observation: White and light-blue text sits on a dark panel while selected rail controls and keyboard focus gain a clear outline. The generic geometry can be distinguished against the room floor and wall.

consistency.observation: New desk and the same transform controls appear in both layouts. The contextual editing vocabulary matches the hints over the desk and floor on desktop.

states.observation: The room first identifies approximate editable Bedroom geometry. The generic desk addition appears afterward, and the saved screen restores the same rendered room and Desk Map with working revision 3.

responsive.observation: The narrow view exposes Spatial context and a single feature panel, with the canvas available when it closes. The reduced-motion phone recording traverses this path and returns to the canvas after reload.

keyboard.observation: The visible result of the Escape and Shift+F10 sequence is the focused Authoring mode selector and the subsequently saved draft. The actions are identified in the replay steps rather than inferred from a static image alone.

focus.observation: Spatial context has an obvious active outline. The phone and desktop saved captures retain a visible focus ring on the Authoring mode selector during the keyboard save journey.

feedback.observation: The feature panel confirms Added a generic desk and explains adjusting position and dimensions. The final editor shows Working draft saved. Measured feedback is about 324 to 477 ms against a 3000 ms budget.

motion.observation: Normal desktop sampling shows editing, a reload and restoration of the same geometry. Reduced phone sampling shows that the same correction and saved return are readable with reduced motion.

continuity.observation: Desk Map and the Bedroom remain associated after reload, and the saved desktop view retains the extra desk. The Creator returns to the Studio Library on both widths.

complexity.observation: Room feature selection and disclosures put correction commands in a dedicated surface. On mobile the route from room editing to Spatial context and back to the model takes a panel switch, but each sheet gives the room and feature names.

role-outcomes.observation: The formal replay shows the Creator adding a generic desk, seeing rendered geometry, restoring it after reload, saving and returning. In the independently inspected exact-source supplement, parametric-bound-support-protected.png and parametric-bound-rebuild-protected.png show the warning to move the attached object and the unchanged reference desk. Parametric-known-measurement.png shows the 1.95 m Width reference and scaled room. Parametric-restored-room.png and parametric-phone-reloaded.png show the saved sofa after desktop and phone reload. The focused case passed its stored width and reference checks and verified phone draft persistence.

fallbacks.observation: The direct room editor remains usable while the fixture shows AI unavailable. In the exact-source attached-support supplement, the Inspector explicitly directs the Creator to move the attached object to a different surface before removing or rebuilding the desk. Ordinary save and reload remain available.

composition.observation: The desktop Inspector sits beside the intact cutaway room. The phone presents the disclosure, disabled chooser, consent and manual fallback in a single narrow pane with the same account and editor shell around it.

hierarchy.observation: Under Scene settings and Environment, Room photograph reconstruction precedes the provider warning, then upload and privacy controls. The manual editing route is stated in the warning before the disabled action.

typography.observation: The disclosure title and unavailable notice read as distinct lines; the photo file limits and consent text use quieter body copy. The bottom of the disclosure focus border crowds the first explanatory line on the phone.

spacing.observation: The picker, permission checkbox, privacy details and Reconstruct room stay visibly separated. The introductory line immediately below the focused summary needs more clearance from its focus ring.

controls.observation: The native disclosure opens, the photo picker and reconstruction action show disabled styling, and the permissions and privacy details remain visible. Creator Studio remains a way back to Library.

contrast.observation: The provider warning and manual editing statement read clearly against the dark Inspector. Reduced contrast on Choose Files and Reconstruct room conveys that they are inactive.

consistency.observation: Desktop and mobile use the same readiness language, file information and explicit permission text. Both maintain the Scene settings identity and return to the green Studio Library.

states.observation: The viewer sees Photo import is not configured, no selected file and an inactive reconstruction action. The cutaway persists on desktop and the final frame returns to the Studio Library.

responsive.observation: On the phone the pane fits the viewport width and the full provider explanation, consent and Guided fallback are visible in the screenshot. Desktop can show the editor canvas and the open disclosure together.

keyboard.observation: The disclosure is a named interactive summary and gains visible focus on opening. This sampled journey exercises opening and return; it does not establish keyboard traversal of a configured upload form.

focus.observation: A bright outer ring makes the focused summary unmistakable. Its bottom border nearly overlaps the first explanatory line, but does not obscure which disclosure is active or the separate provider notice.

feedback.observation: The warning explains the actual provider limitation and availability of manual room editing, with the disabled actions supporting the message. Captured feedback is about 104 to 118 ms against the 3000 ms budget.

motion.observation: Normal desktop and reduced phone samples show the same provider decision after opening the disclosure and the same return. Neither sample depends on an animated or simulated import outcome.

continuity.observation: Opening the unavailable feature leaves Desk Map and the rendered room intact. The same Creator account reaches the Studio Library afterward without any upload or inference having started.

complexity.observation: One disclosure groups the readiness explanation, form, consent and details. The refusal appears before the unavailable controls, so the user can decide to keep editing manually without working through the form.

role-outcomes.observation: The Creator can understand the missing provider and see the permission requirement before upload. The unavailable flow leaves the scene intact and returns to Studio. Configured import, inference and room accuracy are outside this packet.

fallbacks.observation: Provider refusal is explicit rather than a stalled submission. The ordinary room remains shown alongside it on desktop; the narrow Inspector also states that manual editing remains available and exposes Guided fallback separately.

findings.observation: On desktop and phone, the bottom edge of the photo disclosure focus ring touches or slightly crosses the first line of its introductory guidance. The individual words, provider warning and disabled controls stay readable, so the issue is visual spacing.
